meta.title: What do in 1 day in Da Nang, Vietnam (Son Tra Peninsula)
meta.description:
🙋🏼‍♂️Traveling to Vietnam? Join my travel group here⬇️
https://www.skool.com/travel-vietnam-6703
✅Local Recommendations🍺☕🛵🍜
✅Travel Guides and tips
✅Meet-up opportunities with fellow Travelers

The Son Tra Peninsula in Da Nang, Vietnam is one of the most under-rated spots in the city. You can easily spend an entire day driving around and exploring. We had a coffee at Son Tra Marina before stopping by the famous Lady Buddha, the tallest buddha statue in all of Vietnam. Finally, we cooled off at a hidden beach called Ca Chuon. This is definitely one of my new favorite spots in Da Nang.

comments.author: @jimreynolds1540
comments.text: Came across your channel on Monday. Great content. E-visa vlog was great, I followed along while watching and you made it easy to fill out visa form. Condo tours are good too. I went to Da Nang back in 1993 to check for surf. I can't believe how it has developed, nothing was there back then. I stayed out by Marble Mountains and every morning school kids would give me a tour through the caves to  practice their English.  These two cousins that worked for Vietnam Air would (borrow) a company van for 4-5 hours a day and take up and down the coast, Hoi An to Hue looking for waves to surf and site-see. I remember awesome looking beaches between Da Nang and Hue we couldn't get to. I'm starting my slow-travel-life on the 27th, Vietnam is first 3 months, be in Da Nang first week of September. Thanks for the content.

comments.author: @mfj2648
comments.text:
Travis - excellent update about this "secret beach" up on the Son Tra Peninsula. When I was in Da Nang back in April (to escape the crazy Songkran water fights here in Thailand where I currently live) I rode my motorbike (rental) several times out to the end of the road - Intercontinental juncture and I noticed along the way little small clusters of motorbikes grouped on the roadside near many different cliffs, and I suspected that underneath these cliffs was many different wonderful beaches - So Travis, I guess that you found one of these hidden wonderful secrets?

Travis - when the road ends at the Intercontinental - there is a guard (at where the road ends and not where the entrance to the Intercontinental is) - someone told me that you can continue onto that road to go further out onto the Peninsula, BUT they only let people go who have powerful motorbikes and not the typical city motorbikes.  Do you know anything about this?  And what is beyond the Intercontinental on that gravel road?  I want to discover this additional secret when I return to Da Nang next year --> unless of course you discover it first :>))
